# When Do the Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Under the EU AI Act Apply?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally required obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence). Following a "Digital Omnibus on AI" amendment process agreed by the Council and Parliament and formally in force since 27 July 2026, this deadline has been extended, and current official EU guidance confirms the Annex III obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence). Separately, high-risk obligations for systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I apply later, from 2 August 2028 (high confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
As adopted in 2024, the AI Act set obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems to apply from 2 August 2026, 36 months after entry into force [EU AI Act implementation timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline) (high confidence). This date was widely cited across compliance guides and legal trackers prior to the amendment process [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026) (high confidence).

### The Omnibus Amendment Process
A "Digital Omnibus on AI" legislative proposal to amend the high-risk timeline was adopted on 19 November 2025 [Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai) (medium confidence). On 7 May 2026, the Council and Parliament reached political agreement to extend the high-risk rules timeline — originally proposed by the Commission to extend by up to 16 months — contingent on confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools were available [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules) (high confidence). The resulting AI Omnibus regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 [EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) (high confidence).

### Current Applicable Deadline
Following the Omnibus amendments, official EU guidance confirms that obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from **2 December 2027** [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) (high confidence). Separately, high-risk obligations for AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I will apply later, from 2 August 2028 [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [EU AI Compass timeline](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html) (high confidence). The consolidated EUR-Lex text confirms operators of high-risk systems placed on the market before this new application date are subject to transitional rules, with special provisions for systems undergoing significant design changes [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727) (high confidence).

Notably, 2 August 2026 remains active as the deadline for other obligations unaffected by the Annex III extension, including Article 50 transparency duties, AI literacy requirements, and certain enforcement provisions [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [EU AI Compass timeline](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html) (high confidence).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A significant contradiction exists between mainstream guidance and one low-authority source: a news blog claims a "final text agreed in September 2026" pushed the Annex III deadline further to 2 August 2029, citing continued unreadiness of harmonised standards [AI Act news blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update) (low confidence). This claim is uncorroborated by any official EU source and conflicts with the EUR-Lex consolidated text dated 27 July 2026, which reflects 2 December 2027 as the operative date. It should be treated with strong skepticism.

Several undated or pre-Omnibus sources still describe 2 August 2026 as the active Annex III deadline [Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20); these are superseded by the Omnibus's entry into force and later official confirmation of 2 December 2027.

Two additional low-confidence claims are flagged: a February 2025 start date for Chapters I–II with certain prohibitions deferred to 2 December 2026 [Article 113 analysis](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113) (low confidence, 0.12), and a claim that absent Omnibus approval, the original 2 August 2026 date would serve as a legal backstop [LinkedIn commentary](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO) (low confidence, 0.12).

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise official citation number for the AI Omnibus regulation is inconsistently referenced across sources, leaving the exact legal instrument unclear. It remains unclear whether all Annex III obligations (versus specific sub-provisions like Article 6(5)) are uniformly deferred to 2 December 2027. The interaction between the "significant design changes" trigger and the new deadline for systems already on the market requires clarification. Finally, whether readiness of harmonised standards and notified bodies could trigger further delays before 2 December 2027 or 2 August 2028 take effect remains an open question.

This report was produced by an automated research pipeline: web search, source classification, confidence scores computed from source authority, recency and corroboration, and an automated review against the extracted claims.

### Original Timeline
As adopted in 2024, the AI Act set obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems to apply from 2 August 2026, 36 months after entry into force [EU AI Act implementation timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline) (high confidence). This date was widely cited across compliance guides and legal trackers prior to the amendment process [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance), [McKenna Consultants](https://www.mckennaconsultants.com/eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-a-technical-readiness-guide-for-august-2026) (high confidence).

### The Omnibus Amendment Process
A "Digital Omnibus on AI" legislative proposal to amend the high-risk timeline was adopted on 19 November 2025 [Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai) (medium confidence). On 7 May 2026, the Council and Parliament reached political agreement to extend the high-risk rules timeline — originally proposed by the Commission to extend by up to 16 months — contingent on confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools were available [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules) (high confidence). The resulting AI Omnibus regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 [EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) (high confidence).

### Current Applicable Deadline
Following the Omnibus amendments, official EU guidance confirms that obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from **2 December 2027** [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Shaping Europe's Digital Future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) (high confidence). Separately, high-risk obligations for AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I will apply later, from 2 August 2028 [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [EU AI Compass timeline](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html) (high confidence). The consolidated EUR-Lex text confirms operators of high-risk systems placed on the market before this new application date are subject to transitional rules, with special provisions for systems undergoing significant design changes [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727) (high confidence).

Notably, 2 August 2026 remains active as the deadline for other obligations unaffected by the Annex III extension, including Article 50 transparency duties, AI literacy requirements, and certain enforcement provisions [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/faq), [EU AI Compass timeline](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html) (high confidence).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
A significant contradiction exists between mainstream guidance and one low-authority source: a news blog claims a "final text agreed in September 2026" pushed the Annex III deadline further to 2 August 2029, citing continued unreadiness of harmonised standards [AI Act news blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update) (low confidence). This claim is uncorroborated by any official EU source and conflicts with the EUR-Lex consolidated text dated 27 July 2026, which reflects 2 December 2027 as the operative date. It should be treated with strong skepticism.

Several undated or pre-Omnibus sources still describe 2 August 2026 as the active Annex III deadline [Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20); these are superseded by the Omnibus's entry into force and later official confirmation of 2 December 2027.

Two additional low-confidence claims are flagged: a February 2025 start date for Chapters I–II with certain prohibitions deferred to 2 December 2026 [Article 113 analysis](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113) (low confidence, 0.12), and a claim that absent Omnibus approval, the original 2 August 2026 date would serve as a legal backstop [LinkedIn commentary](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO) (low confidence, 0.12).

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise official citation number for the AI Omnibus regulation is inconsistently referenced across sources, leaving the exact legal instrument unclear. It remains unclear whether all Annex III obligations (versus specific sub-provisions like Article 6(5)) are uniformly deferred to 2 December 2027. The interaction between the "significant design changes" trigger and the new deadline for systems already on the market requires clarification. Finally, whether readiness of harmonised standards and notified bodies could trigger further delays before 2 December 2027 or 2 August 2028 take effect remains an open question.
